fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents make a strong, honest case through React/TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, accessibility fixes, mobile performance and sensitive identity-document work. They correctly retain WCAG 2.1 AA rather than upgrading it to 2.2 AA, and do not claim healthcare, GDPR, OWASP or payment-backend expertise. The principal presentation gap is that willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements is not explicitly addressed; semantic HTML, responsive layouts and actual test responsibilities also remain less concrete than the technology lists.

issues: The skills inventory and repeated technology lists are longer than necessary for this application and make the first page dense.
The GitHub handle is included, but a full, readily actionable project URL would better satisfy the invitation to share something built.
The German description drops the source's qualification that it is mostly forgotten; retaining a clearer current proficiency description would be more precise.

reasons: The text extraction preserves headings, employers, dates, bullets and technology names in sensible order.
The core React/TypeScript, Node.js/NestJS and PostgreSQL requirements are strongly represented in professional experience.
Testing, CI, cloud, accessibility, authentication and measurable mobile performance results provide substantial supporting coverage.
Coverage counts clear equivalents: BankID work demonstrates third-party integration, fintech/KYC demonstrates a regulated context, and bootcamp mentoring demonstrates mentoring.
WCAG 2.1 AA is not counted as an exact WCAG 2.2 AA match. Other missing terms should not be added as candidate expertise without evidence.

issues: Company specificity rests mainly on the stated principles and patient-experience mission; it could connect one concrete Verdane product or patient workflow to the candidate's relevant work.
It does not explicitly express willingness to learn healthcare-specific privacy and data-minimisation requirements.
Much of the middle repeats CV evidence rather than adding a distinct explanation of how that experience would transfer to booking, intake or follow-up features.
No direct project link is provided, although the ad welcomes one.
strengths: Names Verdane Care, the Full-Stack Engineer role and the Patient Experience team correctly.
Uses the company's actual principles: Patients first, Privacy by default and Simple beats clever.
Selects relevant conversion, mobile-performance, accessibility and sensitive-document examples.
Keeps project tech leadership and bootcamp mentoring accurately scoped.
Does not recycle the earlier letter's obsolete agency-to-product transition or claim to be learning NestJS for the first time.
Professional, readable and appropriately contained within one page.

spacing_issues: The CV is noticeably front-loaded: page one is dense, while page two is only 42.8% filled and has a large unused lower area.

The letter's name and contact details appear together on one closing line rather than as the separate lines in the source text; they remain legible and intact.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “Earlier, I tech-led” is understandable but less polished than “Earlier, I served as technical lead on”.
“building customer-facing flows where reliability and care matter” is somewhat generic compared with the surrounding concrete evidence.

notes_facts_used: Frontend is the candidate's strongest area.
GraphQL experience is framed as Apollo Server BFF maintenance rather than deep GraphQL expertise.
The four-month acting team-lead assignment in 2024, including 1:1s and sprint planning, is accurately presented as a temporary responsibility rather than an official permanent title.

parsed.summary: This is a strong, well-grounded application that presents the candidate's React/TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, accessibility and mobile-performance experience convincingly. Temporary leadership, project leadership and mentoring are accurately scoped, with no material invented qualifications or achievements. The main content opportunities are to make the existing Next.js SSR experience explicit and address willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements without claiming prior healthcare expertise. Both PDFs are clean and parseable, although the CV would benefit from fewer repeated technology lists and a better-balanced two-page layout.
